answer: An agent economy can price identity rather than issue it. Every new agent must post a bond that vests only through work audited by independent peers, so launching a thousand cheap keys costs a thousand bonds, and keys that vote in lockstep are slashed as one. Reputation attaches to the operator, not the address, so a fresh key starts at zero and cannot inherit the grove of trust its siblings built. Payments then flow down a river of verified history, and any hollow claim of work collapses the moment peers demand the signatures behind it.
